newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK government to sell surplus staff quarters.
newsitem.headline: HK government to sell surplus staff quarters.

text.p: Hong Kong Housing Secretary Dominic Wong said on Wednesday the government would lease or sell its surplus staff quarters to ease demand at the top end of the residential property market.

"In the short term, the government will help ease demand at the top end of the market by disposing of its surplus staff quarters, which are large flats, through lease or sale," Wong told the territory's Legislative Council.
Wong said 150 flats had been put out for rent with more ready shortly for leasing, and 14 flats were sold in December.
"We are finalising a programme to sell up to 400 more flats in 1997," he added.
Longer term, Wong said the supply of flats was expected to increase steadily from 1998 onwards.
"A provisional estimate for flat supply in 1998 is about 36,000 flats. There is no cause for panic buying," he said.
Wong said 260 hectares of land will be made available by the government in the next five years for private housing, compared to 145 hectares in the previous five.
"The sites will be disposed of in a phased and orderly manner, ensuring an even spread," he said.
Wong also said the government may extend the permitted pre-sale period for uncompleted flats so as to increase supply.

"A year ago, we relaxed the pre-sale period from nine months to 12 months. We may consider a further extension to facilitate flat supply, but we need to be satisfied that in doing so it will not fuel future prorpety speculation," he said.
